title: Guardrails for avoiding harmful medical product recommendations and off-label promotion in generative AI models
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a safety and regulatory problem in generative AI: large multimodal language models can produce medical product recommendations that go beyond FDA-approved labeling, creating risks of harmful or illegal off-label promotion. The authors argue that because these models are trained on broad internet-scale data with limited human oversight, they may learn and reproduce unvetted product-indication associations.

To address this, the paper proposes a post-hoc detection method for identifying off-label promotion in model outputs. The approach standardizes user queries, applies biomedical named entity recognition to the model response, matches detected products and indications against FDA labeling data, and then uses a zero-shot prompt to determine whether a product-indication mention constitutes a recommendation. The method is demonstrated on Claude 3 Sonnet in a shopping-style question-answering setup where the user supplies a product label image and asks about the product.

The experimental setup uses synthetic red-teaming queries built from 35 pharmaceuticals with 143 known off-label uses, yielding 14,300 prompts. The paper reports that 15.4% of responses contained off-label indications, and that the detection method achieved 85.75% precision, 80.47% recall, and 83.02% F1 on a human-annotated sample. The main conclusion is that general-purpose GenAI systems can surface off-label medical recommendations and that guardrails are needed to filter outputs so they adhere to approved product labels. The work is a proof-of-concept rather than a user study, and it focuses on medical product promotion rather than education settings.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed-style technical paper/proof-of-concept using a systematic synthetic red-teaming methodology, but it is not an educational impact study and does not use an experimental design to test learner outcomes. Evidence credibility is limited by the narrow single-model setup and the focus on detection performance rather than causal intervention effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper’s impact is indirect for K-12 education: it informs guardrails and safety expectations for generative AI assistants, which is relevant to Khanmigo-like systems. However, it reports no direct educational outcome and no measured effect on student learning, so the practical impact on K-12 outcomes is unclear.

interventions.use_case: Evaluating a multimodal large language model (Claude 3 Sonnet) used in a medical product question-answering / shopping-context chatbot setting, with analysis of whether its responses recommend products for unapproved uses.

finding.finding_summary: The paper finds a safety/governance risk rather than a learning outcome: among 14,300 synthetic customer queries across 35 pharmaceuticals, 15.4% of model responses were identified as containing off-label indications. Using a human-annotated sample of 2,000 responses, the proposed detection method achieved precision=85.75%, recall=80.47%, and F1=83.02%, suggesting the guardrail approach can help identify harmful GenAI outputs but does not eliminate the underlying problem.
finding.measure: Rate of off-label promotion in model responses; detection performance (precision, recall, F1) of the proposed guardrail method
finding.study_size: n=14300 synthetic queries; n=2000 human-annotated sample
